fi-centropyge-bicolor.title: Bicolor Angelfish
fi-centropyge-bicolor.summary: A dwarf angel, yellow in front and deep blue behind. Not a reliable reef fish.
rows: With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods and mysis or other frozen shrimp
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Samoan and Phoenix Islands, north to southern Japan, south to New Caledonia; throughout Micronesia
notes: Wants lots of rock for grazing and hiding (70 gal or more).

fi-centropyge-bispinosa.title: Coral Beauty Angelfish
fi-centropyge-bispinosa.summary: One of the most popular dwarf angels: deep blue with orange-yellow flanks. Hardy, but may nip corals.
rows: With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods and meaty frozen foods
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to the Tuamoto Islands, north to the Izu Island, south to Lord Howe Island
notes: Needs a 70 gal or larger tank with rock to graze.

fi-centropyge-eibli.title: Eibl's Angelfish
fi-centropyge-eibli.summary: A dwarf angel from the eastern Indian Ocean, also sold as the Red Stripe Angelfish.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. May nip sessile invertebrates and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae and mysis or other frozen shrimp
Eastern Indian Ocean: Sri Lanka to Western Australia, including Indonesia and the Andaman Is
notes: Wants a 70 gal or larger tank with plenty of live rock.

fi-centropyge-vroliki.title: Half Black Angelfish
fi-centropyge-vroliki.summary: A dwarf angel that is pearly in front and black behind.
rows: Keep it as the only dwarf angel in the tank
With caution. May eat soft coral polyps, zoanthids and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae and mysis, plus live rock to graze
Western Pacific: Christmas Island in the eastern Indian Ocean and Bali to the Marshall Islands and Vanuatu, north to southern Japan, south to Lord Howe Island
notes: Wants 70 gal or more with lots of hiding places.

fi-chaetodontoplus-mesoleucus.title: Singapore Angelfish
fi-chaetodontoplus-mesoleucus.summary: A butterflyfish-shaped angel with a black eye mask, white front and dark body. Can be hard to settle in.
rows: About 7 in; wild record 18 cm (7.1 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Grazes microalgae, filamentous algae and diatoms; also offer meaty and angelfish foods
Indo-West Pacific: Japan to Indonesia, Sri Lanka and east to Papua New Guinea
notes: Some refuse food at first; a quiet tank with calm tankmates and hiding places helps.

fi-centropyge-heraldi.title: Herald's Angelfish (Yellow Angel)
rows: With caution. May nip large-polyp stony corals, some soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods and meaty items
Indo-Pacific Ocean: from Sri lanka and Bali to the Indo-Malay archipelago to the Marshall Islands
notes: Wants 70 gal or more with plenty of live rock to graze.

fi-centropyge-loricula.title: Flame Angelfish
fi-centropyge-loricula.summary: A popular red-orange dwarf angel that adapts well to aquarium life, but it may nip corals.
rows: About 4 in; wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
With caution. Prone to nip stony and soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore. Spirulina, marine algae, angelfish foods, mysis or other frozen shrimp and meaty foods
Pacific Ocean: mainly in tropical waters
notes: Needs 70 gal or more with lots of hiding places and live rock to graze.

fi-genicanthus-lamarck.title: Lamarck's Angelfish
fi-genicanthus-lamarck.summary: A silver-gray swallowtail angelfish striped in black, one of the few angels where males and females look different (the female has one bolder stripe into the tail). It feeds on plankton in open water, so unlike most angels it is considered reef safe.
rows: About 9 in; wild record 25 cm (9.8 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one male; a male with a few females works in a big tank
Plankton-eater in the wild: spirulina and marine algae, angelfish foods, mysis and other frozen shrimp
Indo-West Pacific: Indo-Malayan region, eastward to Vanuatu, north to southern Japan, southward to the Great Barrier Reef
notes: May chase small, timid plankton-eaters such as anthias, fairy and flasher wrasses and firefish.

fi-centropyge-flavissima.title: Lemonpeel Angelfish (Christmas Island)
fi-centropyge-flavissima.summary: A bright yellow dwarf angelfish with sky-blue rings around the eyes and blue fin edges. It grazes algae more than most angels.
rows: About 5 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
Best kept singly; it fights with other dwarf angels
Omnivore that needs more algae than most angels: spirulina, marine algae and seaweed, angelfish foods, mysis and other meaty items
notes: Give lots of live rock to graze on.
This SKU is sold as a Christmas Island fish.
warn: Not reliably reef safe: it nips large-polyp stony corals, soft corals and clam mantles.

fi-centropyge-argi.title: Cherubfish (Atlantic Pygmy Angelfish)
fi-centropyge-argi.summary: A tiny deep-blue and orange dwarf angelfish from the Caribbean and western Atlantic. Feisty for its size, it grazes algae and may pick at some corals and clams.
rows: Can be very aggressive toward other fish for its size
With caution (often fine, but may nip clams and some corals)
Algae grazer: spirulina and algae-based foods plus small meaty foods like mysis and brine shrimp
Western Atlantic: Bermuda and Florida to French Guiana, incl. the Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean
notes: Needs plenty of hiding places in the rockwork, especially at first.
Feed several times a day until it settles; an established tank with algae growth helps.

fi-centropyge-nox.title: Midnight Angelfish
fi-centropyge-nox.summary: An all-black dwarf angelfish from western Pacific outer reefs. Hardy and active, it grazes algae but may pick at some corals and clams.
rows: Semi-aggressive; keep one dwarf angel per tank
With caution: may nip stony corals and clam mantles
Omnivore: spirulina and algae-based foods, angelfish formulas and mysis, about three times a day
Western Pacific: Ryukyu Islands to Indonesia, the Solomons, the Great Barrier Reef and New Caledonia; coral-rich outer reef slopes, 3–70 m
notes: Does best in an established tank with algae growth and plenty of live rock caves.

fi-centropyge-flavopectoralis.title: Yellowfin Pygmy Angelfish
fi-centropyge-flavopectoralis.summary: A dark dwarf angelfish with yellow pectoral fins from the Indian Ocean. Like other dwarf angels it grazes algae, needs rockwork to hide in, and may nip some corals.
rows: Semi-aggressive; keep one dwarf angel per tank
With caution: may nip stony corals and clam mantles
Omnivore: spirulina and algae-based foods plus mysis and other meaty foods several times a day
notes: Lives in harems in the wild; dwarf angels start as females and the dominant fish can turn male.

fi-apolemichthys-xanthurus.title: Xanthurus Angelfish (Cream / Indian Yellowtail Angel)
fi-apolemichthys-xanthurus.summary: A lattice-patterned cream-and-black angelfish with a bright yellow tail from the Indian Ocean. Hardy and fairly peaceful for an angel, but it may nip soft corals and clams.
rows: Semi-aggressive; territorial toward other angelfish. One per tank
With caution: may nip sessile invertebrates, soft corals and clam mantles
Omnivore: spirulina and algae plus frozen meaty foods, several times a day
notes: Give it plenty of live rock with algae and hiding places.
Add it before or with other angelfish species, not after.
